## Status and authority

This is the main acceptance procedure for plan `support-native-mission-budget-custody-2026-11-13` and rubric `acceptance-support-native-mission-budget-custody-2026-11-13`. It explains how to execute and interpret the existing criterion procedures together. It does not change their Intent, Acceptance, methods, required scopes, thresholds, or passing ratings.

The procedure is prospective. At authorship the plan is a draft and its runtime cases are planned/unknown. This document supplies no implementation, test-execution, native/provider, credential, privilege, spend, activation, or release authority. Establish the separate admission and resource authority for each execution before using the corresponding step. A signed acceptance-contract amendment is not permission to exercise the native route.

## Build the complete evidence inventory

Enumerate every criterion and all named check cases from the current rubric. Follow any pagination to completion. Record each case's owning criterion, maintained file, execution status, required evidence plane, exact scope and subject fingerprints, and evidence reference. Keep the source inventory intact: any bounded display or execution batch must expose what remains and a continuation followed to the end. Never turn a display limit into a coverage claim.

## Source identity and lifetime accounting

Execute the R-1 and R-2 procedures against the same retained source. Capture before/after source registration and consumed reservation/resource history together with the isolated targets' own rows. Exercise the canonical absent/wrong binding and frozen-policy refusals, concurrent full-window attempts across target databases, and the additional attempt from a recreated target.

Measure success, failure, unknown outcome, duplicate attempt identity and verified-zero cancellation according to the canonical lifetime policy. Preserve exact identities and counts. In particular, an observed failure or uncertain send is not permission to replenish a lifetime request. Prove that target recreation and case isolation cannot manufacture a new mission budget. Use the rubric's exact boundary cases and limits, not a current fixture's more convenient defaults.

## Source isolation and origin qualification

Treat R-4, R-7 and R-8 as distinct outcomes even where their maintained harness is shared: trusted parent custody/secret isolation, bounded authenticated target reference, and honest evidence scope. Inspect only redacted presence predicates. No source credentials, mission control, final-send callback, host witness or privilege artifact may be accepted from, or leak through, the worker IPC path.

Keep the following observations separate and give each its own recorded evidence:

- R-11 validates a trusted harness-created synthetic witness bound to actual fixture creation and the exact source, parent, database, manifest and policy. Run its valid control and each forged, replayed, pre-existing/uncreated and mismatched counterpart through the same maintained validator.
- R-12 validates the authenticated current privilege artifact's exact source/parent/child binding, both verifier roles, enforced isolation policy and measured ambient-identity source-authentication failure. Run the valid artifact and every missing, malformed, stale, foreign or mismatched counterpart through that same validator.
- R-10 measures host-derived origin/branch selection, consuming those separately validated results. Retain its unknown/unproven-origin and caller/configuration-label refusals and all negative cases transferred from retired R-13. There is no second R-13 rating.
- R-9 measures the actual real-source custody/privilege boundary, consuming artifact-validation and origin-selection results without rating them a second time.

A synthetic witness or artifact fixture is a contract check. Label synthetic evidence configuration-isolation / synthetic-source-only; it cannot establish real-source custody or privilege isolation. A real-source outcome requires separate authorized execution and independent exact-child, both-role proof that the child's ambient OS identity fails source-store authentication under the enforced boundary. A separate UID or NoNewPrivs declaration alone, or merely omitting a DSN, is insufficient. Retain the exact child and verifier identities in secure provenance while exposing only redacted predicates in ordinary evidence.

Both deny-all and allow-all implementations must fail the appropriate valid/invalid counterpart controls at each maintained boundary. Use the maintained test framework and the repository's copy-out mutation procedure when falsifiability needs a mutation; never mutate the shared tree as a probe.

## Target authority, receipts and lifecycle prerequisites

Before measuring composed final send, execute R-22's maintained unit and real-PG matrix. Prove the exact APPLIED target operation, work-item, worker and source binding and a separate refusal for each canonical negative class. Canonical APPLIED target authority is not replaced by a matching-looking caller label.

Execute the lifecycle criteria through the canonical producer groups and the two named facade invokers specified by the current plan and Decisions. Preserve those populations exactly. A direct canonical writer remains pull-only unless the governed contract explicitly says otherwise.

Keep distinct observations for R-5's correlated native-completion barrier; R-14's separate clean-completion result; R-15's next-admission refusal; R-16's residual receipt validity; R-17/R-18's refusal to equate a durable mutation with acknowledgement or cleanup; R-19's single upstream send per receipt; R-20's composed earliest deadline and no renewal; and R-21's committed cancellation outside caller-owned transactions.

For the configured facade invokers, observe durable request, authenticated notification, exact parent-epoch advance, both-controller invalidation and correlated barrier acknowledgement in the specified order, with cleanup measured separately. Inject source ACL/grant revocation, desired-revision replacement, cancellation and claim release/transfer after every await, including the last target database read, and prove the applicable no-send result after the matching acknowledgement. Direct canonical writers instead prove their specified pull-only next-admission refusal and residual authority window; do not call their durable mutation completed native revocation.

Retain crash, loss, restart, replay, expiry, forged/stale/successor, double-callback/send and earliest-issuance cases. A caller-owned transaction rollback produces no facade request, barrier acknowledgement or parent-epoch change; an external transaction commit stays pull-only. Fresh authorization requires fresh complete source authentication and target pull with ordinary lifetime accounting, not renewal of an already reserved attempt.

## Compose both final-send gates

After the prerequisite results above exist, execute R-3's two-database composition. Independently invert target-operation/P009 capacity and retained-source capacity. Both gates must authorize the same authenticated attempt with identical identity, body and credential through the synchronous final-send boundary.

Measure the phase-specific residue rather than treating every refusal as interchangeable. For the source-refused additional attempt, preserve the deliberately committed target per-attempt row and receipt-level hosted/P009 hold, with no new source reservation or upstream send and unchanged earlier source history. A fresh receipt creates its own hosted hold; reusing the receipt preserves its existing hold and does not create another per-attempt hold.

Distinguish source refusal before reserve from expiry after source commit. The latter retains its consumed source lifetime slot and token history even with no send. Do not refund those histories or label intentional target-before-source residue a leak. R-20 owns expiry enforcement, R-19 receipt single-use, R-22 target binding, and R-5 the barrier/no-send observation. R-3 cites their independently recorded results as prerequisites and does not rate those outcomes again.

## Evidence records and acceptance

For every measured case retain its canonical criterion and case identity, maintained suite/run reference, actual pass/fail/skip/error status, exact source/target/parent/child/attempt/receipt and policy fingerprints, applicable authority, before/after redacted ledgers, phase and barrier/deadline observations, evidence plane and scope qualification. Keep positive controls, negative counterparts and failed attempts. Never print credentials or replace an intact identity with a truncated string.

Emit repeatable measurements through the registered checks and results ledger. Preserve the complete inventory across batches and restarts and explicitly account for anything unmeasured. Each observation has one primary outcome owner; another criterion may consume it as a prerequisite without receiving a second rating for the same outcome.

Obtain current independent rubric critique through the canonical vetting policy. After implementation and current measured proof exist, complete the per-item code-truth audit and route independent acceptance grading through the normal plan workflow. A planned case remains unknown even if the rubric is well specified. The implementer records the acceptance call only after reading independent evidence, and the plan's activation, grading and shipment gates remain separate. Report contract readiness, synthetic configuration evidence, real-source qualification and shipped behavior using their actual evidence scopes.

## Why this is a separate runbook

The canonical criterion fields carry the detailed executable contracts. This curated procedure supplies the cross-criterion ordering, custody and interpretation that cannot be inferred from a list of checks alone. It intentionally references current canonical identities and inventories so it cannot silently become a competing copy of the contract.
